reading.quote: As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another.

reading.p: We cannot build anything extraordinary in life alone. As the sayings go, "Rome was not built in a day," and Rome was not built alone. A CEO runs a company, but it is the employees who keep it alive. Steve Jobs would not have become who he was without Steve Wozniak.
We can only go so far on our own, so we should not let pride fool us. There is wisdom in the saying, "If you want to go fast, go alone; if you want to go far, go together."

reading.h2: We Were Designed to Be Together, Not Alone

reading.p: We were designed for one another. Consider the most basic human bonds: a woman and a man joined by vows make a marriage; a woman, a man, and children make a family; a sister and a brother make siblings. What do marriage, family, and siblings all have in common? Each one is built on relationship and togetherness.

reading.quote: It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make a helper suitable for him.

Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their labor: If either of them falls down, one can help the other up. But pity anyone who falls and has no one to help them up. Also, if two lie down together, they will keep warm. But how can one keep warm alone? Though one may be overpowered, two can defend themselves. A cord of three strands is not quickly broken.

reading.p: Relationships are not easy. The best relationships take time, energy, sacrifice, compassion, and love. People are difficult because people have feelings, opinions, and beliefs of their own.
A good question to ask ourselves is: how do you want to be remembered by people? Our words and actions outlive us.

reading.quote: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.

reading.p: The old saying "sticks and stones may break my bones but words will never hurt me" is a great misconception. Our words have the ability both to build and to destroy. The lesson recalls the "water crystal experiment" conducted by Masaru Emoto as an illustration of how powerfully words can affect what is around us.

Who are you? Imagine being asked, "I need one brave volunteer"—the way we answer reveals how we see ourselves. Our identities are made up of our thoughts, beliefs, and actions. As one philosopher put it, "We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit."
You have the power to choose. Who do you choose to be?

reading.quote: Watch your thoughts, they become your words; watch your words, they become your actions; watch your actions, they become your habits; watch your habits, they become your character; watch your character, it becomes your destiny.

reading.p: Uplift the people around you. Do not look down on people unless you have a hand reaching down there to help them up. Choose compassion over judgment, for compassion kills judgment. Step into the other person's shoes; compassion brings forth understanding.
Remember not to teach someone how to swim when they are drowning. Iron sharpens iron, but a dull blade cannot sharpen a dull blade. To help and sharpen others, we ourselves must be sharpened first.

studyGuide.overview: Drawing on Proverbs 27:17, this lesson teaches that we are designed for community and cannot grow or accomplish great things alone. It explores the power of our words to build or destroy, the way our thoughts and habits form our character, and the call to lift others up with compassion rather than judgment.
keyPoints: No one succeeds entirely alone; we were created for relationship and togetherness.
Scripture affirms that two are better than one and a cord of three strands is not quickly broken.
Relationships require time, energy, sacrifice, compassion, and love.
Words carry real power, holding both death and life; they can build or destroy.
Our identity is shaped by our thoughts, beliefs, habits, and actions, and we have the power to choose who we become.
We are called to be the difference by lifting others up with compassion over judgment.
Iron sharpens iron: we can only sharpen others when we ourselves are being sharpened.
reviewQuestions: What does the proverb "As iron sharpens iron" mean for our relationships?
Why does the lesson say there is no such thing as a "one man army"?
What does Ecclesiastes 4:9-12 teach about the value of companionship?
How do our words have the power of life and death, according to Proverbs 18:21?
How do thoughts and habits shape our character and identity?
What does it mean to choose compassion over judgment, and why must we be sharpened to sharpen others?

checks: Scripture (Proverbs, Genesis, Ecclesiastes) used for moral instruction, consistent with Orthodox teaching on community and love.
Theme of togetherness and self-giving love aligns with the Orthodox emphasis on communion and unity.
No doctrinal claims about the nature of Christ, the Trinity, or the saints are made; nothing contradicts the Tewahedo faith.
Secular illustrations (Rome, Apple, the water crystal experiment, philosophers) are used as moral analogies, not as doctrine.
